If the preferred lifetime was less than the minimum required lifetime
ipv6_create_tempaddr would error out without creating any new address.
On my machine and network
column2: this error happened immediately with the

column1: preferred lifetime set to 1 second
column2: after a few minutes with the

column1: preferred lifetime set to 4 seconds
column2: and not at all with the preferred

column1: lifetime set to 5 seconds. During my investigation
Exchange post from another person who seems to have had the same
problem: They stopped getting new addresses if they lowered the
preferred lifetime below 3 seconds
column2: and they didn't really know why.

column1: The preferred lifetime is a preference
kernel does not strictly forbid new connections on a deprecated address
nor does it guarantee that the address will be disposed of the instant
its total valid lifetime expires. So rather than disable IPv6 privacy
extensions altogether if the minimum required lifetime swells above the
preferred lifetime
column2: it is more in keeping with the user's intent to

column1: increase the temporary address's lifetime to the minimum necessary for
the current network conditions.
With these fixes
column2: setting the preferred lifetime to 3 or 4 seconds ""just

column1: works"" because the extra fraction of a second is practically
unnoticeable. It's even possible to reduce the time before deprecation
to 1 or 2 seconds by also disabling duplicate address detection (setting
/proc/sys/net/ipv6/conf/*/dad_transmits to 0). I realize that that is a
pretty niche use case
column2: but I know at least one person who would gladly

column1: sacrifice performance and convenience to be sure that they are getting
the maximum possible level of privacy.
